The paper proposes a novel metamaterial absorber based on Minkowski fractal patch configuration for X-band applications.
The proposed absorber achieves broader absorption bandwidth with minimum thickness.
The Minkowski fractal patch configuration is a fractal model constructed using a recursive procedure.
The indentation factor (i/j) affects the resonant frequency and space filling property of the fractal.
Several unit cells with dimensions optimized for resonance at closely spaced frequencies are used in the proposed absorber.
The optimum thickness of the substrate is 0.4 mm.
Configuration#2 has increased absorption with a wider bandwidth compared to configuration#1.
The MSK patch with the least reflection coefficient resonates at 9.9 GHz.
The percentage of power absorbed by configuration#2 over a bandwidth of approximately 1 GHz is greater than 75%.
The paper uses full wave simulation software to analyze the performance of the proposed absorber.
The substrate is made of commercially available FR-4 material.
The metallic portions of the absorber are modeled using copper layer of thickness 0.02 mm.
The parametric study is carried out to identify the optimum thickness of the substrate.
The paper compares the absorption characteristics of configuration#1 and configuration#2.
The proposed absorber has a miniaturized RAS model with substrate thickness not exceeding 0.4 mm.
The paper uses Minkowski fractal geometry in the design of the absorber.
